scenes.title: Get engineering data into your own system
scenes.subtitle: Sync vendor APIs without maintaining one ingestion script per tool.

scenes.description: This demo uses the bundled GitHub simulator. No real vendor account or token is involved.

scenes.title: Run a pull-request sync
scenes.subtitle: The real CLI fetches data and writes records to the Postgres sink.
scenes.label: First sync
scenes.description: One GitHub operation reads three simulated repositories. These are event records, not a count of unique PRs.
scenes.footer: Actual CLI and Postgres results · bundled simulator · illustrative rendering, not a shipped UI

scenes.title: Query the records that landed
scenes.subtitle: Use the sink data to answer your own questions.
scenes.label: Postgres result
scenes.description: Group stored records by repository and select merged events. Vendor payloads retain their own shapes inside a common envelope.
scenes.footer: Actual CLI and Postgres results · bundled simulator · illustrative rendering, not a shipped UI

scenes.title: Progress survives the CLI process
scenes.subtitle: Each sync saves a per-repository cursor in the store.
scenes.label: Saved progress
scenes.description: The first CLI process exits. The next process can read its stored progress without starting the history walk over.
rows: Before the first PR sync: no cursor
After the sync: cursor data persisted
scenes.footer: Actual CLI and Postgres results · bundled simulator · illustrative rendering, not a shipped UI

scenes.title: The next sync resumes from that cursor
scenes.subtitle: A second CLI process completes against the same simulator data.
scenes.label: Resumed sync
scenes.description: The eight records are boundary replays. All eight already existed in the sink; the Postgres sink updates their existing rows.
rows: same per-repository cursor as the first run
scenes.footer: Actual CLI and Postgres results · bundled simulator · illustrative rendering, not a shipped UI

scenes.title: Choose where records go next
scenes.subtitle: Run sync now, schedule it with serve, or embed the runner in Go.
scenes.label: Your data
scenes.description: This walkthrough used Postgres. Delivery can replay records, so consumers need to deduplicate when their sink does not do it for them.
